central_claim: The published FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency mechanism, measured on other FET fusions in other diseases, is only WEAKLY supported when tested for internal consistency and transfer to EMC in public data (structural precondition splits by fusion type, EMC tumour transcriptomes show only generic proliferation elevation, and drug-response/dependency correlations fail 3 of 4 mechanism-specificity tests), so no EMC-specific ATR vulnerability is established and the wet-lab ask stands unchanged as a hope rather than a finding.

blockers.summary: Part D's newly-added machinery-control finding is stated as a sweeping claim about 'every null part D reports on the drug-response axis' but the document does not apply that discount to Part D's other null rows elsewhere in the same section and in Sec 6.1 -- an internal inconsistency about how much each Part D null should be trusted.
blockers.evidence: Sec 5 (new content in this commit): '...the artifact's verdict is `INSTRUMENT_CANNOT_DETECT`. Part D's ATM row is therefore UNINFORMATIVE, not negative, AND EVERY NULL PART D REPORTS ON THE DRUG-RESPONSE AXIS BOUNDS LESS THAN THIS DOCUMENT HAS BEEN CLAIMING.' -- read literally this covers all of Part D's negative findings on the drug-response axis, not only the ATM-status stratification row. Yet two paragraphs later, still in Sec 5, the replication-stress row is narrated at full strength with no such caveat: 'Since the fixed grading's WEAK tier is precisely "only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes are elevated," a predictor that cannot beat a proliferation gene set has not demonstrated a mechanism.' The held-out FET-fusion-signature row is likewise treated as a settled negative ('The held-out FET signature reproduces the PARP bound rather than escaping it... tracks ATR-inhibitor sensitivity at rho -0.138 and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity at -0.239'), again with no reference to the machinery-control caveat. Sec 6.1's own accounting of 'what bounds real' ('the bound is on ONE side, not three... Part D's ATM row correlates transcript abundance... bounds the proxy') discusses only the transcript-abundance ATM row (a different, earlier test from the predictor table) as discounted, and is silent on the replication-stress and held-out-signature rows -- i.e. it still implicitly counts those as informative.
blockers.fix: Narrow the scope of the 'every null part D reports... bounds less than claimed' sentence to what the machinery-control test actually validated -- the genetic-mutation-status stratification design (ATM-status and the BRCA2/PARP control), not the continuous rho correlations used for the replication-stress and held-out-FET-signature rows, which are a different statistical design the BRCA2 control did not test. Alternatively, if the intent really is that the whole residual space is suspect, explicitly extend the same 'uninformative, not negative' caveat to the replication-stress and held-out-FET-signature rows in Sec 5 and to Sec 6.1's 'what bounds real' paragraph, so the discount is applied consistently rather than only where it happens to be introduced.

p1s.summary: Sec 7's provenance claim ('nothing is hand-typed here that the artifact does not carry') is stated without qualification, but the commit's own message documents an unresolved structural gap -- an artifact can be rewritten under a converged hardening round without any digest tracking the drift -- which is exactly the failure this commit's change (1) had to fix after it already happened once (the stale Sec 0 provenance cell that five blind seats missed because deliverable_digest binds only to the manuscript's own bytes). The manuscript's confidence language does not reflect that this alignment is currently verified by manual audit only, not continuously, and the same class of staleness could recur silently before the next audit.
p1s.evidence: Sec 7: 'Provenance. Every number above is produced by emc_atr_vulnerability.py and lives in its JSON artifact; nothing is hand-typed here that the artifact does not carry, and --check re-derives all of it offline from the committed inputs cache.' Commit message (3dcb494fa): '...an artifact can be rewritten UNDER a converged round without moving any digest, and clause 1 keeps printing OK... Left as an open question with three candidate answers on the row, not answered by inventing a gate.'
p1s.fix: Add a one-line caveat to Sec 7 (or Sec 0's banner) noting that artifact-manuscript alignment is verified at correction time by manual audit, not by an automated digest, and that this document has already been caught out of sync with a rekeyed artifact once (Sec 0's superseded provenance cell, this commit).

p1s.summary: The 'type 2 holds against 4 of the 4 measured types' framing in the Sec 0 headline table, while accurate and adequately hedged in its immediate context, is a strong-sounding fragment that could be quoted out of context (in a collaborator package, outreach draft, or a future summary) as validating the structural precondition more broadly than the document's own WEAK/no-EMC-specific-finding framing supports, since it is the second-commonest rather than the commonest EMC fusion.
p1s.evidence: Headline table: 'Type 2 holds against 4 of the 4 measured types, type 1 against 1 -- a tie with EWSR1::ATF1 exon 10 at 0.267 -- and type 5 against none.' This sits inside a cell that also states, correctly and prominently, 'Met for one of the two commonest fusions and not for the other,' and the document elsewhere is careful to say the commonest fusion (type 1) is the one that fails. The risk is only that the '4 of 4' phrase is quotable in isolation, not that this document itself misuses it.
p1s.fix: No change strictly required inside this document; if the '4 of 4' figure is ever copied into a shorter summary (outreach draft, collaborator package abstract), pair it with the 'commonest fusion fails' qualifier in the same sentence rather than relying on surrounding paragraphs.
